statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail 14% (low), Stress 41% (moderate), Confidence 87% (high). Shared assessment for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD.
recommendation: Tail sits in the low band, so the mapped state remains EA_ON. The basis is a fourth observed rejection of the session high rather than an absence of evidence: the Nasdaq-100 has held below its 30,699.00 record for about two hours, NQ futures are some 56 points under 30,997.00, and neither extreme has extended. VIX at 14.26 is down 4.1% and printing at its session low, while the tape is rotational rather than aligned, with the Dow down 0.48% against a Nasdaq Composite up 0.33%. Two scheduled items sit unresolved inside the current hour, the 2-Year note auction and Fed Barkin's remarks, and the narrow danger window stays on the 23 September US cash open and flash PMI cluster, the only forecast hour that reaches the caution band.
headline: The Nasdaq-100 has spent roughly two hours rejecting its 30,699.00 record high, with VIX falling to a session low and the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq pulling in three different directions.
body:
Tuesday's US cash session has now produced a fourth failure to extend, and that is what holds this assessment in the low Tail band. At the assessment cutoff the Nasdaq-100 is 30,640.83, up 0.52%, sitting 58 points under the 30,699.00 intraday record and 144 points above the 30,496.43 open, which is also the day's low. December NQ futures are 30,941.00, up 0.51%, 56 points under their 30,997.00 high. Both highs are unchanged across two consecutive hourly assessments, so the index has repeatedly advanced into its record and been turned back rather than accepted above it. Mean reversion is working, and the session-extreme-holding and shallow-pullback conditions that a higher Tail score would require are absent.

Cross-asset evidence points the same way rather than aligning behind a single direction. VIX is 14.26, down 4.1% and printing at its 14.22 session low, so implied volatility is decaying while the index sits near a record. Index dispersion is unusually wide: the Dow is down 0.48%, the S&P 500 is flat at -0.02%, and the Nasdaq Composite is up 0.33%, which is the signature of rotation rather than an index-level trend. The 10-year yield is 4.98%, up about 1.7 basis points and at the top of a 4.926 to 4.980 range, so the 5% marker is close but there is no rate impulse for equities to trend on; the 2-year is near 4.78% and little changed, although readings for the front end were not fully consistent across sources this run.

The geopolitical channel has turned two-way rather than one-way. WTI is 91.25 dollars, down 1.21%, and Brent is 99.88 dollars, down 0.46%, but Brent had traded as low as 97 dollars before recovering above 100 after President Trump told the UN General Assembly he faces a decision on whether to pursue a deal with Iran or annihilate the country, and that any deal is more likely after the November midterms. Earlier reporting that Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if US military pressure eases had driven the earlier weakness. Oil giving back most of a sharp decline within one session is itself evidence of a two-way headline channel rather than a directional one. Delayed Finviz context was only partially available and older than the freshness threshold this run, with its futures and calendar sections missing, so it was not relied on; the megacap and semiconductor sections it did carry were consistent with the rotation described above.

Stress is 41%, in the moderate band, reflecting an index at record levels, a 10-year yield pressing 5%, an unresolved 2-Year auction inside the current hour and live Middle East diplomacy with a genuinely two-way headline channel, none of which currently translate into a pathological price path. Confidence is 87% because the price, volatility, rate and oil readings were all taken live within minutes of the cutoff, tempered slightly by one inconsistent 2-year reading and by the auction result not yet being published.

The 24-hour outlook keeps Tail between 11% and 21%. The remaining US cash hours rise modestly to 17% through the power hour and the 20:00 UTC close, then fall through the thin overnight window to a floor of 11%. The profile rebuilds through the European session on Wednesday and peaks at 21% in the hour following the S&P Global flash PMI at 13:45 UTC, which lands 15 minutes after the US cash open and is joined by Fed Governor Barr at 14:05 UTC and EIA crude stocks at 14:30 UTC. That single hour is the only one to reach the caution band and carries the WATCH mapping; the danger window is drawn narrowly around that cluster, from 13:30 to 14:30 UTC, rather than across the whole session.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours contain a complete set of 24 published hourly assessments, none of them revised with later information. Monday's late US session carried Tail in the elevated band at 30 to 33% under a trend-up mode, then stepped down to WATCH at 23% and into the low band at 14% as that session closed. The overnight and European hours held Tail between 11% and 13% in a normal mode. Tuesday's US open lifted Tail to 21% and WATCH for one hour on an opening push, after which successive rejections of the record high returned it to 17% and then 15% under a mixed mode in the two hours before this assessment.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour outlook keeps Tail inside an 11 to 21% band, and only one forecast hour reaches the caution band. The remaining US cash hours rise modestly from 14% to 17% through the power hour and the 20:00 UTC close, then fall through the post-close and Asian hours to a floor of 11%. The profile rebuilds gradually through the European session on Wednesday and peaks at 21% with a WATCH mapping in the hour after the S&P Global flash PMI at 13:45 UTC, an hour that also carries Fed Governor Barr at 14:05 UTC and EIA crude stocks at 14:30 UTC. It eases to 18% and then 16% in the final hours on the assumption that post-event price discovery is orderly. Confidence decays from 87% to 68% across the horizon as the live evidence behind this assessment ages.

forecast.analysis: Observed now: NDX 30,640.83 (+0.52%) is 58 points under the 30,699.00 record high and 144 above the 30,496.43 open/low; NQ 30,941.00 sits 56 under its 30,997.00 high. Both highs are unchanged for about two hours. VIX 14.26 (-4.1%) is at the session low. Two-way balance keeps Tail in the low band.

NDX mid-range: 58 pts below the high, 144 above the 30,496.43 low

news.title: Stock market today: Dow slips, Nasdaq and S&P 500 drift higher as oil pares losses after Trump's UN address

forecast.analysis: First hour after the 2-Year auction and Barkin remarks. Tail edges up one point only because the absorption of that supply is not yet observable. A move toward the caution band would require a yield jump that equities then extend on without retracing, which the flat front end has not so far produced.
drivers: Condition to watch: auction tail feeding a 2Y yield jump equities trend on
10Y near 4.98% and at the top of its 4.926-4.980 range; 5% is the marker
Baseline assumption: orderly absorption, consistent with a little-changed 2Y
Invalidation of balance: NDX reclaiming and holding above 30,699.00

forecast.analysis: US power hour. Late-session positioning can remove two-way trade faster than midday, so the conditional risk is a close-driven push that runs without meaningful pullbacks. Tail is lifted modestly for that structural reason alone, not because such a push has been seen; the session so far has rejected its high repeatedly.
drivers: Power hour: late positioning can compress retracements into the close
Checkpoint: whether the record high is tested a fourth time or abandoned
Rotation out of the Dow would have to broaden before Tail could build
No scheduled US macro release inside this hour

forecast.analysis: The 20:00 UTC cash close. Index-level imbalance at the closing auction is the main conditional path to a one-way finish; an orderly close instead lets Tail decay into the evening. Scores are held level with the power hour because neither outcome is observable yet.
drivers: US cash close at 20:00 UTC; closing-auction imbalance is the swing factor
Record-high close versus a second consecutive rejection is the checkpoint
VIX decay into the close would corroborate an orderly finish
Conditional: a late oil headline re-pricing the risk-appetite channel

forecast.analysis: Post-close hour before the futures maintenance break. Liquidity thins and the cash reference disappears, so directional continuation normally loses its engine here. Tail steps back toward the overnight baseline on the assumption that the close passes without a disorderly imbalance.
drivers: Cash market shut; NQ futures become the only price-path reference
Thin post-close liquidity historically favours two-way, low-follow-through trade
Assumption carried forward: an orderly 20:00 UTC close
Headline channel stays open via Middle East and US-China summit coverage

forecast.analysis: CME maintenance break and reopen. The gap across the halt is the only structural risk in this hour, and it needs a genuine headline to matter. Absent one, the reopen typically prices close to the prior settle and Tail continues to decay.
drivers: CME futures maintenance halt and reopen inside this hour
Conditional gap risk across the halt requires a fresh headline to activate
No scheduled US macro release in this window
Baseline: reopen near the prior settlement with thin two-way trade

forecast.analysis: Late US evening into the Asian handover. This is typically the thinnest stretch of the 24-hour cycle, where even a sizeable move tends to retrace rather than extend. Tail sits near its overnight floor.
drivers: Thinnest liquidity window of the cycle ahead of the Asian handover
Low participation normally produces retracement rather than extension
Watch item: any Iran or Strait of Hormuz headline reaching the oil tape
No scheduled US macro release in this window

forecast.analysis: Asian session opens. Japanese and Korean cash trade give NQ futures a fresh reference, and semiconductor names there can transmit tone into the Nasdaq complex. A one-way path would require that transmission to be both aligned and sustained, which is uncommon in this window.
drivers: Tokyo and Seoul cash open; Asian semis are the main transmission channel
Condition for Tail to build: aligned, sustained Asian chip-sector direction
Oil's overnight path remains the secondary risk-appetite input
Baseline mode stays normal on thin, two-way overnight structure

news.title: Nasdaq notches record-high close, AI optimism reignites, Treasury yields retreat

forecast.analysis: Mid Asian session. With no scheduled catalyst and the US tape closed, the forecast assumes range-bound overnight trade; this is the floor of the 24-hour Tail profile rather than a judgement that risk has disappeared.
drivers: No scheduled US macro release in this window
Floor of the forecast Tail profile on absence of catalysts, not absence of risk
Asian equity tone carried forward from the prior hour
Invalidation: a gap that holds without retracement into the European handover

forecast.analysis: Asian afternoon. The conditional risk here is an unresolved geopolitical headline arriving into thin books, which can move price sharply without the depth to sustain it. Scores are held at the overnight floor.
drivers: Thin books amplify headline moves but rarely sustain them
Middle East diplomacy remains the live two-way headline channel
No scheduled US macro release in this window
Assumption: no overnight escalation; revised on any confirmed development

forecast.analysis: Late Asian trade into the European pre-open. Direction set here is frequently reversed once European cash arrives, so persistence rather than magnitude is the condition that would matter for Tail.
drivers: Late-Asia direction is often reversed at the European cash open
Persistence, not magnitude, is the condition that would lift Tail
No scheduled US macro release in this window
Carry-forward: VIX at session lows, supportive of mean-reverting trade

forecast.analysis: European pre-open. Overnight positioning begins to unwind and volumes build. Tail starts its gradual rebuild from the overnight floor purely on returning liquidity and the approach of the Wednesday event block, not on any observed structure.
drivers: European pre-open; volume and depth begin to rebuild
Rebuild reflects returning liquidity, not observed directional structure
Wednesday flash PMI at 13:45 UTC becomes the session's anchor checkpoint
Overnight gap versus the 30,496.43 US open is the first reference to check

forecast.analysis: European cash open. Index futures usually find a firmer reference here. A trend condition would need the European open to extend an overnight direction rather than fade it, which has not been the recent pattern in this cycle.
drivers: European cash open provides the first firm reference of the day
Condition: European open extending, rather than fading, overnight direction
Recent sessions have repeatedly faded overnight direction at this hour
No scheduled US macro release in this window

forecast.analysis: Early European session. Tail continues its measured rebuild as the day's structure forms. The relevant conditional check is whether NQ establishes a directional bias here that survives into the US pre-open, or simply ranges as it did overnight.
drivers: Checkpoint: does an early European bias survive into the US pre-open
Range-bound European morning would keep Tail near the low-band floor
European macro prints can set tone but rarely drive NQ one-way alone
No scheduled US macro release in this window

forecast.analysis: Mid-morning Europe. Historically a two-way stretch for NQ. Tail stays low because the amplifiers that would justify more, shallow pullbacks and repeated extension after failed retracements, are conditional here rather than observed.
drivers: Required amplifiers remain conditional, not observed, in this window
Shallow pullbacks plus repeated extension is the pattern that would lift Tail
European mid-morning is historically a two-way stretch for NQ
No scheduled US macro release in this window

Mixed mode reflects two competing references, not conflicting evidence

forecast.analysis: European midday. Risk builds gradually into the Wednesday US block. A one-way path is conditional on pre-positioning that carries through the PMI rather than reversing on it, which is the less common outcome.

Condition: pre-positioning carrying through the PMI instead of reversing

Proximity to the 13:45 UTC PMI is the sole reason for the increment

forecast.analysis: Final hour before the US cash open. Pre-positioning into the flash PMI block dominates. Tail rises modestly on the approach; a material step higher would require the pre-open to show a one-way bid or offer that holds into the release rather than balancing.
drivers: Last hour before the 13:30 UTC cash open and the 13:45 UTC PMI
Step higher requires a one-way pre-open that holds into the release

forecast.analysis: US cash open at 13:30 UTC followed by the S&P Global flash PMI at 13:45 UTC. The opening auction and a Tier-1 release land inside fifteen minutes, so mode is event/whipsaw. Tail is raised for the structural collision, not for a predicted outcome; the release result is unknown at the assessment cutoff.

Raised for structural collision, not for any predicted release outcome
Opening-auction continuation without pullbacks is the key condition
Whipsaw around the print is the base case, not sustained direction

forecast.analysis: Peak of the 24-hour profile and the only hour that reaches the caution band. Post-PMI repricing, Fed Governor Barr at 14:05 UTC and EIA crude stocks at 14:30 UTC stack inside one hour. The concern is a delayed second leg after the initial reaction, which is where the mapped state moves to WATCH.
drivers: Three catalysts stack: post-PMI repricing, Barr 14:05 UTC, EIA 14:30 UTC
Mapped policy state for this hour: WATCH (Tail in the 20-24 caution band)
Mechanism of concern: a delayed second leg after the first reaction
Danger window 13:30-14:30 UTC is drawn narrowly around this cluster
De-escalates quickly if price discovery is orderly and retracements occur

forecast.analysis: First hour after the event cluster. Tail falls back below the caution band on the standard assumption that post-event price discovery is orderly, volatility decays and retracements resume. That assumption is conditional and would be revised against the observed path.
drivers: Assumes orderly post-event discovery with retracements resuming
Conditional: revised upward if extension continues without pullbacks
VIX decay after the print is the corroborating signal to watch
Exits the caution band as the catalyst stack clears

forecast.analysis: Wednesday midday, the final hour of this horizon. Tail settles back toward the session baseline as the morning catalysts are absorbed. Confidence is at its lowest here because every live reading behind this assessment is then roughly a day old.
drivers: Final hour of the horizon; morning catalysts largely absorbed
Confidence floor: live evidence is roughly 24 hours old by this point
US 5-Year note auction follows later at 17:00 UTC, outside this hour

forecastDetail.comment: Balanced midday tape: the 30,699.00 record high has been rejected repeatedly and is unextended for about two hours, VIX is at its session low, and index dispersion is wide. The 2-Year auction and Barkin remarks land inside this hour but are unresolved.

Post-auction absorption is the open question. Tail edges up one point on that alone; the flat front end gives no rate impulse for equities to trend on, and reclaiming 30,699.00 would be the structural invalidation.

Power hour. Late positioning can compress retracements into the close, which is why Tail is lifted modestly. Nothing of that kind has been observed; the session has so far rejected its high on every test.
The 20:00 UTC cash close. A closing-auction imbalance is the conditional path to a one-way finish, while an orderly close lets Tail decay into the evening. Scores held level pending that outcome.
Post-close thinning removes the cash reference and normally drains directional follow-through, so Tail steps back toward the overnight baseline on the assumption of an orderly close.
